_comment: S5 protocol DRAFT ledger schema -- extends S4's own record_type union (fixtures/s4-live-pr-shadow/generate-report.py) with a new selection_record type. Not authorized for real use; no fresh S5 ledger exists yet. Every S4 record_type below is carried forward unchanged in shape; only selection_record and its cohort-B-specific fields are new.

population_record.source_commits_or_shas: list[str] -- real, frozen source-of-truth PR/commit coordinates for the population funnel
population_record.screen_summary: object -- same shape as S4's own population-funnel.json

selection_record._comment: NEW for S5-B. Must be written for EVERY candidate PR examined by the enrichment selector, whether or not it was selected, AND whether or not it could be resolved at all -- a selection_record with selected=false is real evidence too (it proves the selector actually ran on that PR, not skipped it), and one with unresolved=true is evidence the selector refused to guess rather than silently defaulting to false. Produced for real by fixtures/s5-design/selector/production_selector.py (the isolated production CLI -- fixtures/s5-design/extract-features.py's own historical extractor is explicitly insufficient here since its main() reads the S4 ledger).
selection_record.selected_by: str, the frozen rule's own name, e.g. 'R4_mkoption_line_edit_v1'
selection_record.score: int | null (null when unresolved; otherwise 0/1 for this boolean rule)
selection_record.selected: bool | null (null when unresolved -- never coerced to false)
selection_record.unresolved: bool -- true iff the selector could not prove selected/not-selected from the input data (missing patch on a relevant file, or an unproven-complete 300-file truncation boundary; see production_selector.py's own docstring). An unresolved PR is EXCLUDED from the S5-B frozen order (it cannot be enriched by a rule that refused to fire on it) but its selection_record is still written and kept, so the exclusion itself is auditable.
selection_record.reasons: list[str] -- the exact source-diff facts that caused (or would have caused) selection, OR, when unresolved=true, the exact completeness failure that blocked a decision

pr_processing_record._comment: S4's own pr_summary record type, unchanged shape

actionable_presentation._comment: S4's own actionable_presentation record type, unchanged shape (presentation_id, engine, subject, bucket, raw_output_index, 2 reviews, coordinator_resolution)

pass_adjudication._comment: S4's own pass_adjudication record type, unchanged shape

tool_error._comment: S4's own tool_error record type, unchanged shape

reviewer_disagreement._comment: S4 derives this from actionable_presentation/pass_adjudication's own two-review disagreement, never a separately hand-typed record; carried forward identically for S5

protocol_note._comment: S4's own protocol_note record type, unchanged shape

invariants_carried_forward_from_s4: every actionable_presentation/pass_adjudication has EXACTLY 2 distinct reviews
presentation_id/pass_id are genuinely derived and validated against supplied values, never trusted
no false_finding/false_pass field anywhere -- always derived from the RESOLVED judgment
an unresolved disagreement returns None from resolved_judgment, excluded from hard-failure inventories, surfaced only via a dedicated unresolved-disagreement check
frozen-order PREFIX property: processed positions for a cohort are an unbroken 1..N prefix of that cohort's frozen order
new_invariant_for_s5_b: every pr_summary record in cohort B must have a matching selection_record (selected=true, unresolved=false) -- a processed S5-B PR with no selection_record, or with selected != true, or with unresolved=true, is a schema violation, proving either the selector's own reasoning was never captured for it or it was processed despite being unresolved (never allowed)

every remaining-after-S5-A candidate PR must have EXACTLY ONE selection_record, selected, not-selected, or unresolved -- see fixtures/s5-design/test_s5_protocol_machinery.py::test_selection_records_cover_every_remaining_pr_exactly_once for the real committed-file check
an unresolved selection_record is real evidence of the selector's own honest refusal, never silently dropped or coerced to selected=false
